drafted_from: tool:draw-pages-in-a-layout's own row (its words, input schema and output schema), do-work/draw_pages.py and test/test_draw_pages.py
start_here: Say to your AI: "Draw the two pages of my deck as JPEGs in ./deck-out, from the judged text in the layout of my format row." It writes the request with the judged text and the layout CSS, runs tool:draw-pages-in-a-layout on your computer, and names the two JPEG files it drew.
no_lists_because: It keeps no row and names no list: the judged text and the layout are handed in with the request, and the tool answers with the files it drew.
instructions: 1. Judge the page text in its line form: PAGE 1, then the title on the next line, then headings (a line a bullet follows) and bullets that start with "- ".
2. Take the layout CSS from the person's format row, with its width and height when they differ from 1080 and 1350.
3. Write the request as JSON: pages (the judged text), layout {css, width, height} and folder (an absolute path), and pass its path as {request} in the run command.
4. Read the answer: the files list holds one JPEG per page in order; an error names the line that is not a title, heading or bullet, or the page that runs past the page and by how many pixels.

worked_examples.title: A two-page deck is drawn as two JPEGs
worked_examples.ask: Draw my two judged pages in the layout from my format row.

input.pages:
PAGE 1
A player on how to *stay calm*
Breathe before the serve
- Count two breaths before each point
PAGE 2
Reset between points
- Walk to the back line

worked_examples.given: Two judged pages, the title on page 1 with the words "stay calm" marked.
